title: Her nonprofit trains rural women to make and sell their own sanitary pads
sources: Forbes, September 2025 - How The Desai Foundation Cultivates Dignity Across Rural India
Ms. Magazine, September 2023 - Empowering Women in India Through Menstrual Equity: The Ms. Q&A With Megha Desai
caption:
Her nonprofit trains rural women to make and sell their own sanitary pads. Not as charity - as a paid job.

Megha Desai is President of The Desai Foundation, a diaspora-founded nonprofit running the Asani Sanitary Napkin Program across 8 Indian states - training local women to manufacture and distribute retail-quality, low-cost pads themselves. Roughly 250 women work as paid door-to-door distributors, retrained quarterly. The Foundation's work has reached millions of lives and was recognized at the Clinton Global Initiative in 2022.

Most menstrual health programs hand out free pads. This one hands out jobs - and lets the pads follow.

Sources: Forbes, Ms. Magazine (2022-2025)

Independent citizen project. Not affiliated with the Government of India.
